data.name: Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links
data.detailed_description:
Take on Duelists around the world with "Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links"!
- Star-studded lineup includes: Yugi, Kaiba, Joey, Mai and more!
- Voices from the anime heighten the Dueling experience!
- Intuitive controls for beginners! The depth to satisfy "Yu-Gi-Oh!" veterans!
- Signature monsters with stunning 3D animations!
- Build your ultimate Deck and aim for the top!

Step into a world that crosses dimensions and connects all Duelists. In Duel World, any location transforms into a Duel Field where heated Duels unfold!

* Japanese text can only be selected if you started the game in Japan.

[FEATURES]

-Duels
The "Yu-Gi-Oh!" TCG (Trading Card Game) can be played digitally with newly designed, intuitive controls optimized for your personal computer! Also, signature monsters like "Dark Magician" and "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" make their appearance with dynamic visuals!



-Single Campaign (Duel World)
Duel as your favorite characters from the "Yu-Gi-Oh!" world and complete Stage Missions to earn various rewards!
New cards can be obtained from the Shop!

-Duelists
Challenge Yugi, Kaiba, Joey, Mai and other Legendary Duelists! Complete specific Missions to unlock and these characters!
Earn Skills and rewards by leveling up your favorite characters!

-Online PvP
With "Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links," engage in heated Duels anytime and anywhere against players around the world! Climb through the rankings and claim the title of King of Games!



-Decks
Build your very own Deck with cards you collect in-game and take on opponents!
Stay tuned for future card additions!



[ABOUT "Yu-Gi-Oh!"]
"Yu-Gi-Oh!" is a popular manga created by Kazuki Takahashi that was serialized in SHUEISHA Inc.'s "WEEKLY SHONEN JUMP" from 1996. Konami Digital Entertainment Co., Ltd. provides a Trading Card Game (TCG) and video games, based on the "Yu-Gi-Oh!" anime series created from the original manga, that are enjoyed around the world.

reviews.review:
[h1]A favorite for anime fans and nostalgic duelists, with a format built around Skills[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]★ 7.5/10 — Three-zone fields and character Skills give it its own style, but BOX pulls raise the cost of getting cards[/h2]

[b]⊕ BEST FOR:[/b] Players who like anime characters and aces, study less popular decks, or play Rush Duel.

[b]⊖ NOT FOR:[/b] Players who want the old rhythm of card-by-card exchanges, change decks frequently, or don't like mobile game dailies.

[b]▣ Critical Benchmarks:[/b] Metacritic iOS 80/100.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]◆ Opening[/h2]

I have been playing Yu-Gi-Oh! DUEL LINKS since the early beatdown days, around the time it launched internationally in 2017. A Level 4 monster could hold the field with 1,700 ATK, and Rex Raptor and Seto Kaiba could use their Skills to start with Jurassic World and Mountain, respectively, to boost ATK. Summon a monster, set Mirror Wall or Enemy Controller, and wait for the other side to attack. As soon as the set card was flipped, you would know whose monster could survive to the next turn.

The game has its own card pool, limits, and Skills. Now I think of it as another kind of Yu-Gi-Oh! If you've played Master Duel or the OCG/TCG, you may recognize the cards, but you have to relearn how to build a deck and play.

[h2]◆ Strengths[/h2]

[b]⊕ The field is easy to read when you start[/b]
Speed Duel has three Main Monster Zones and three Spell & Trap Zones, with 20–30 cards in the Main Deck and four in the starting hand. Both sides start with 4,000 LP, and a direct attack for 2,000 takes half. There is no Main Phase 2.

[b]⊕ With different rules, cards sitting on the bench elsewhere can see play[/b]
Master Duel's ladder matches are decided in one game (BO1), and in a paper BO3 you can swap in Side Deck cards between games. This alone will change what cards you bring. Chazz's Ojama King can lock up to three empty Main Monster Zones. That leaves two open on a five-zone field. In early Duel Links, it could lock all three if they were empty.

The limit system is also something I like very much. Limited 1, Limited 2, and Limited 3 each have a shared quota of 1, 2, and 3 cards, respectively. If your archetype's starter and a generic board breaker are both Limited 2, you can bring one of each or give both slots to one of them.

[b]⊕ Skills can really save some old aces[/b]
When Pegasus plays Toons, he can start with Toon World. Jaden/Yubel's Skill lets you Normal Summon Elemental HERO Neos and Yubel without Tributing, and can also bring out Yubel's next form. When the opponent has a monster on the field, Yusei has a Skill to put three Synchro Monsters on the field as material for Shooting Quasar Dragon.

Sky Striker's Skill can add to the Extra Deck and place a Field Spell. You have to think about the deck and its Skill together.

[b]⊕ It really feels like the anime when you duel[/b]
There are character voice lines for drawing cards, summoning, and attacking. Some cards have special lines, and some aces also have summoning animations. In different Duel Worlds, you can challenge familiar faces at the Gate, unlock characters, and change outfits.

I especially like the music. When an ace is played or LP gets low, the music can change halfway through the duel. When Jaden has the upper hand and that track plays, it really feels like watching him play cards in the anime again.

[b]⊕ If you are tired of Speed Duel, you can switch formats[/b]
Rush Duel, added in 2023, has its own card pool, and you can Normal Summon multiple times in a turn. If you use up your hand, you draw five cards on your next turn. You can play ranked Rush Duels on Steam and mobile. The limited-time Legacy Duels mode offered old decks you could borrow.

Character Deck Duels is permanent. Unlock a character to get a free prebuilt deck with a preset Skill. It has a separate Forbidden/Limited List, and raising the deck's Grade lets you swap up to five cards.

[b]⊕ If you don't play ranked, you can play for a long time for free[/b]
Duel NPCs, do Duel Quizzes, level up characters, and play it as a single-player game. You can save up Gems and Tickets, and anniversary events have given away full Structure Decks.

[h2]◆ Weaknesses[/h2]

[b]⊖ Some Skills are so strong that they can sometimes bypass the rules[/b]
Before its March 2024 nerf, Tachyon Dragon Domination could search the Deck and Set a Level 8 Dragon from hand.

The most annoying thing is what happens after my Droll & Lock Bird resolves. Main Deck draws and searches are blocked for the rest of the turn. Some of the opponent's Skills can still search, and Memento can still draw with its usual DARK Skill. I can't chain to a Skill that puts a monster directly on the field, and my usual summon responses don't work. I can understand giving less popular decks an opener and the second player a way in. But you have cards in hand and never get a chance to use them. After a while, I really feel like I'm playing against Skills.

[b]⊖ BOXes eat a lot of Gems, and switching decks costs more[/b]
It's 50 Gems per pack and 500 for ten. If the only copy of a UR is in the last pack of a 180-pack Main BOX, that's 9,000 Gems. To get three copies, you have to reset the BOX, and one deck often needs cards from several BOXes. Dream Tickets are not issued often, BOX Chips cover a limited selection, and some cards come from events or the Card Trader's rotation.

Excess cards can be converted to Gold, Stones, or Jewels for the Card Trader. Master Duel lets you dismantle unused URs to craft the missing one. If you want to switch archetypes here, you still have to open packs.

[b]⊖ Besides turn order, it depends on who you're up against[/b]
Ranked uses a coin toss for turn order, and the second player draws one more card. Some Skills give the second player extra cards or materials, and Horus has builds meant to break boards going second. I didn't care as much about the coin toss in DL as I did in Master Duel. Memento can pair its 5,000 ATK/DEF Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation with Mementotlan Cranium Burst. Lowering the monster's ATK and DEF by 1,000 negates an opponent's monster effect activated on the field, up to five times in separate Chains. There may be two or three turns in a duel, but the opponent's first turn can take a long time.

[b]⊖ It's easy to learn the rules, but it takes time to keep up in ranked[/b]
If you change the Skill in the same deck, what you save your negate for can also change. Once a Skill or the card limits change, you have to practice your opening plays again and rebuild the deck. At higher ranks, even a familiar deck can struggle against the current top decks.

[b]⊖ The mobile grind is still too heavy[/b]
Standard Duelists take time to respawn unless you spend Duel Orbs. For some events, you have to save up tickets, then duel the same character at the Gate for points. Auto-Duel can play for you, but you still have to enter the event and claim rewards yourself. It felt pretty fresh to unlock characters and get new cards, but doing it all again for a few dozen Gems got tiring. Speed and Rush share Gems, so you have to split your time to build for both. Most of the time I open Master Duel just to play a game. When I open DL, I often check what I have to grind that day.

[h2]◆ Conclusion[/h2]

Almost ten years later, Konami is still adding characters and pushing new modes. If you want to stick with it, think about how much time you have and whether you can adapt to this Skill-heavy format.

Occasionally when I go back to play ranked, I still think of those duels where you played one card and I played one in return. That feeling probably won't come back, but I still think the direction Duel Links has taken makes sense.

[hr][/hr]
